title: Book Three · Chapter 89: Two Saturday Mornings
story:
On Monday, Ronan and Leo ask Mrs Lan about a book table.

They show her the place beside Mr Qiu's stall. It is clear of the doorway. There is room for one small table.

Mrs Lan looks at the two cloth bags.

“How many books?”

“Eighteen,” Ronan says.

“And which days?”

They want the next two Saturday mornings. Those are the second and third Saturdays of the holiday. Leo leaves on the fourth.

Mrs Lan agrees to those two mornings, from nine until eleven. They will keep the books inside their own bags before and after the sale.

Mr Qiu has a small folding table. He can let them use it beside his stall for one yuan each morning. The money covers the table and the little selling space.

“Two mornings, two yuan,” Leo says.

He takes two from their shared envelope and pays Mr Qiu. Ronan writes the cost beneath the bags.

Their shared cash is now twenty-four yuan.

Mr Qiu opens the table. Ronan stands at one side and Leo at the other. The books fit in two short rows, with a clear space between them.

Mrs Lan comes through the gate with a basket. Both boys move their chairs in at once.

She passes easily.

“That space stays,” she says.

Ronan nods. He can see the path from the door to the road.

After they fold the table again, Leo points to the second sale morning on their page.

“Your visit with Anna.”

“The third Saturday. I need to be at the library by nine.”

“I can be here with Mr Qiu.”

“I can help set out the bags first. Then I will leave at half past eight.”

Leo checks the table time. “We open at nine. I can do that part.”

Ronan writes his leaving time beside the visit. The two boys look at both mornings before they put the page away.

Mum has made her own plans for those Saturdays. Some customers will collect at the house. She will carry another finished piece herself. Ronan's delivery work will be lighter during the sale.

That afternoon, the boys put the books back on the dry shelf. The bags are clean now, and the folding table stays with Mr Qiu.

Leo taps the cash envelope.

“Twenty-four left. We haven't sold one book.”

“The table is very rich,” Ronan says.

Leo laughs. They go outside with the football for half an hour. Ronan has enough numbers on the page for today. On the grass, he only needs to count the boys on his side.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

folding table＝折叠桌；selling space＝摆卖位置；set out＝摆出来；half past eight＝八点半。

## 理解问题

1. 谁同意使用位置和桌子？时间、费用各是什么？
2. 第三个星期六，Ronan原本怎样安排参观和书摊？是谁在九点开卖？

## 读句子

**Their shared cash is now twenty-four yuan.**

拆开看：Their shared cash / is now / twenty-four yuan.

他们的共同现金／现在是／二十四元。
